subject: Post-call: matching latency & throughput constraints to cost levers
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@optiven.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + SLO matrix (latency/throughput)

Thanks for the call earlier, Jordan — good to align on the high-level goals. Quick recap and three asks so we can size a pilot and an estimate: 

Call highlights
- Primary workload: conversational search for product catalog + short-form summarization fallback.
- Target p95 latency: 180–220ms for prompt->first-token (interactive search).
- Streaming use: yes, for the conversational UX; typical response lengths 80–250 tokens.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions with peaks to 300 for sale events.
- Throughput expectation: ~20k tokens/minute steady, burst to 50k tokens/minute.

What we attached: SLO matrix (sheet per route) — fill the yellow columns with realistic per-route % of traffic and average response length. That will let us pick model families + batching profiles.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) You: confirm per-route traffic split and typical response lengths in the sheet (OptiVen Product Search / Summarize / Rerank).
2) You: confirm whether end-to-end latency SLO is strict for first-token or can be p99 for full response for summarization.
3) We (Redwood): produce a short cost vs SLO matrix showing which levers to use (continuous batching, prefix caching, 8-bit quantization, smaller model variant for rerank) and propose an initial reserved-capacity size for a 3-week pilot.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sizing call next week (Mon/Tue) to review the filled matrix and go over a sample request trace. Vanessa will join to cover pilot ops and onboarding.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

[Attachment: optiven_slo_matrix.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 48 KB)]
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@optiven.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@optiven.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 18:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + SLO matrix (latency/throughput)

Thanks Markus — appreciate the concise recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- We'll update the sheet by EOD Monday. Traffic split (estimate): Product Search 65%, Summarize 25%, Rerank 10%.
- Response lengths: Search responses average 120 tokens, Summaries average 180 tokens, Rerank is token-light (<30 tokens).
- Streaming: Search and Summaries must start streaming first-token within that 180–220ms p95 target (customers expect immediate typing feedback). Full-response p99 can be relaxed to 800ms for Summaries.
- Concurrency note: 120 steady is accurate for most days; black-friday style peaks could be 600 concurrent sessions (we can’t commit that often but need a fallback path).

One more ask: are you able to include a recommended model-path that prioritizes latency (smaller ensembled model for search + full-quality summarizer behind model-routing) vs a cost-first path?

I'll fill the sheet and tag the specific routes. Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Product, OptiVen
jordan.lee@optiven.com

On Sat, Jun 5, 2027 at 15:02, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the call earlier, Jordan — good to align on the high-level goals. Quick recap and three asks so we can size a pilot and an estimate: ...
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@optiven.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + SLO matrix (latency/throughput)

Great — thanks for the rapid details, Jordan. A few concrete recommendations based on your numbers and the peak/steady split you described: 

High-level decision matrix (latency-first vs cost-first)
- Latency-first path (p95 ~200ms):
  - Model choices: small-LLM-variant tuned for search (quantized 8-bit) for first-token generation, fall back to medium-LLM (fp16) for full summary when quality matters.
  - Levers: continuous batching tuned to 8–12ms batching window, prefix + KV caching for repeated queries, hotspot autoscaling with reserved headroom (commit to Dedicated pool covering 80% steady concurrency).
  - Expected unit cost: higher per-token during steady state but predictable; lower p95 and stable streaming first-token behavior.

- Cost-first path (p95 300–400ms acceptable):
  - Model choices: single medium-quantized model for both routes (heavier batching), more aggressive quantization (4-bit where acceptable), and opportunistic cold-fallback to CPU for low-priority reranks.
  - Levers: longer batching windows, caching only for high-frequency prefixes, dynamic model routing to cheaper variants during off-peak.
  - Expected unit cost: ~30–50% lower but will increase p95 and streaming jitter during bursts.

Recommendations for OptiVen pilot (3 weeks)
1) Start with latency-first for Product Search and cost-first for Rerank. Summaries: start latency-first for primary customer cohort; enable cost-first routing for internal analytics.
2) Pilot capacity: reserve a dedicated pool sized for 150 concurrent steady sessions (20% headroom) with autoscale to burst up to 400 using shared capacity. That addresses typical spikes while keeping predictable baseline.
3) Tuning plan: first week — baseline traffic profile + trace collection; second week — enable continuous batching & KV cache and measure p95; third week — try 8-bit quantized variant for search and compare QA against medium fp16 model.
4) Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback policies to drop to cheaper model variants or route to another region if latency spikes above SLA.

Attachments: I’ve attached a quick cost estimate for the pilot showing per-day token cost ranges for both paths. That includes rough monthly extrapolations if OptiVen committed to a 3-month reserved capacity.

Next steps
- Jordan / Asha: please upload the filled SLO matrix and an example per-route request trace (JSON) to the Drive link.
- Vanessa / Priyom: we’ll convert the recommendation into a one-page Mutual Action Plan and pilot onboarding checklist.
- Schedule: suggest Tue 9am PT for a 30-min sizing call — Vanessa will send a calendar invite.

Thanks again — happy to jump on the call.

Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
